output: We recommend replacing NoteBase with Quill for our 12-member team: Quill delivers significantly faster search, built-in Markdown export, and meets our IT mandate to host all data in the UK—at a predictable cost of £6 per user per month (≈£72/month total). Moving to Quill should eliminate NoteBase’s performance bottlenecks and give us the export flexibility we need without compromising data residency.

Search is now twice as fast when you’re working with large libraries, so finding items takes much less time. You can also export your data in CSV format, and a rare startup crash has been fixed to ensure the app launches reliably.

• Reported total: 350  
Discrepancy: 350 – 330 = 20 (GBP thousand)  
Conclusion: the total should read 330, not 350.

Supported by the two trials  
• Source A (2019, company‐wide, self-reported): employees on a four-day week overwhelmingly “felt” more productive.  
• Source B (2022 pilot, 20 people, no control group): measured output per week held roughly steady under a four-day schedule.

Not established by these trials  
• That a four-day week actually raises objective output (no independent, quantitative gain was demonstrated).  
• That any self-reported boost in productivity translates into higher real-world results.  
• That the findings generalize beyond one company (Source A) or a tiny, uncontrolled sample of 20 people (Source B).
